mechanism: %collect-multisig-sig-pairs (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:295-310) walks the multisig pubkeys in script order and increments a counter, signing only while (< count m); it stops producing pairs at the threshold. Both multisig arms of compute-input-signatures use it -- legacy-multisig (:443-448) and bip143-multisig (:450-456) -- so it feeds the in-place finalizer AND the PSBT signer. Core's SignStep MULTISIG case (refs/bitcoin/src/script/sign.cpp:669-688 at d3056bc) calls CreateSig for EVERY key in vSolutions and caps only the STACK push at required+1, with the comment 'We need to always call CreateSig in order to fill sigdata with all possible signatures that we can create. This will allow further PSBT processing to work as it needs all possible signature and pubkey pairs.' CreateSig records each signature in sigdata.signatures, and PSBTInput::FromSignatureData copies that whole map into partial_sigs (psbt.cpp:178).
consequence: On an m-of-n input where the signer holds k > m keys, walletprocesspsbt and descriptorprocesspsbt record m PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG records where Core records k. The finalized transaction is identical (finalization needs exactly m, and Core's stack cap is the same required+1), so no spend is affected and nothing becomes unspendable -- hence S3. The window in which it is observable is narrower than the finding states, and worth recording: Core's FromSignatureData CLEARS partial_sigs when sigdata.complete (psbt.cpp:163-176), and SignPSBTInput forces complete to false only when finalize is false (psbt.cpp:491), while our %psbt-set-final drops the same records (src/wallet/psbt.lisp:793-805). With finalize=true (Core's RPC default and ours, src/wallet/psbt.lisp:1524) and a complete input the two serialized PSBTs therefore agree. The divergence is real for finalize=false, which is the multi-party workflow the Core comment exists for: a PSBT passed to further cosigners carries fewer signatures than Core would have put there, so a workflow that wants a specific cosigner's signature present, or that later drops one, has fewer spares. When k <= m we produce k pairs, exactly as Core does, so the ordinary single-signer case is unaffected.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3a, warm image. Probe build/ga11probe/p-psbtmulti.lisp drives bl.rpc:compute-input-signatures on a P2WSH m-of-n bare multisig witnessScript with the first HELD keys in the pubmap/keymap, counting input-sig-ecdsa pairs. Controls: (m 1, n 3, held 1) -> 1 pair; (3,3,3) -> 3 pairs; (2,3,2) -> 2 pairs, so the collector does produce more than one pair when it is allowed to. Divergences: (m 1, n 3, held 3) -> 1 pair, Core 3; (m 2, n 3, held 3) -> 2 pairs, Core 3; (m 1, n 2, held 2) -> 1 pair, Core 2. Probe build/ga11probe/p-psbtend.lisp then runs the same cases end to end through the entry point walletprocesspsbt uses -- bl.wallet::%psbt-coins-map plus bl.wallet::%psbt-record-signatures over a hand-built PSBT carrying PSBT_IN_WITNESS_UTXO and PSBT_IN_WITNESS_SCRIPT -- and counts PSBT_IN_PARTIAL_SIG records: (2,3,2) -> 2; (3,3,3) -> 3; (1,3,3) -> 1 (Core 3); (2,3,3) -> 2 (Core 3); no final scriptWitness is set in any case, confirming this is the not-yet-finalized state where Core keeps every signature. Core side read at d3056bc: sign.cpp:669-688 (SignStep MULTISIG), sign.cpp CreateSig, psbt.cpp:161-191 (FromSignatureData) and psbt.cpp:402-511 (SignPSBTInput, in particular :491).
fix_shape: Split the cap from the collection, the way Core does. %collect-multisig-sig-pairs should sign for every held key in pubkey order and return all pairs; the m-of-n cap belongs to %finalize-input-signatures, which already receives the needed threshold in the input-sig struct (src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:322-330) and should take the first m pairs in pubkey order when it assembles the scriptSig/witness -- which is exactly Core's ret.size() < required + 1 push guard, so the in-place spend path stays byte-identical. The PSBT recorder at src/wallet/psbt.lisp:1352-1356 then writes one record per held key with no change, since it already skips a pubkey that already has a signature. Do not also change the finalize-time clearing: %psbt-set-final already matches FromSignatureData's complete branch. A regression test should assert the pair count equals the number of HELD keys for k > m while the finalized witness is unchanged, with the k <= m case kept as a control so a fix that simply removed the cap without touching finalize would still be visible.
